candidates.title: Push and Pull: Elastic Interaction Between Pressurized Spherical Cavities in Nonlinear Elastic Media

requirements.example: neo-Hookean three-dimensional block hole: two equal-sized pressurised spherical cavities in an infinite hyperelastic matrix (interaction energy and driving force vs. separation η/R)

cases.name: neo-Hookean, equal positive pressures P1=P2=P
unlisted_needs: parametric sweep over cavity separation η/R (about 2.2 to 20) and pressure P/µ
driving force = derivative of potential energy with respect to separation
critical separation (η/R)critical where interaction switches from attractive to repulsive
potential energy including the work of the cavity pressure
missing_information: outer domain size used to approximate the infinite matrix
exact pressure range and load steps
normalisation of potential energy and driving force
numerical potential-energy and driving-force values (available only as plots)
whether the boundary is modelled using symmetry or axisymmetry
reference_values: Deformed shape shown for η/R = 2.8, P/µ = 1.0
Interaction attractive for P/µ ≲ 1.0; can become repulsive above a critical η/R for P/µ ≳ 1.0

missing_information: definition of α in terms of C10/C01 (α=1 gives neo-Hookean)
reference_values: Deformed shape shown for η/R = 2.8, P/µ = 1.0

cases.name: Arruda-Boyce (λm=2), equal positive pressures P1=P2=P
reference_values: Deformed shape shown for η/R = 2.8, P/µ = 1.0

cases.name: neo-Hookean, equal negative pressures P1=P2=-P
reference_values: Driving force always negative (attractive) for equal negative pressures
Deformed shape shown for η/R = 2.8, P/µ = 1.0

cases.name: Strain-stiffening sweep (Mooney-Rivlin α, Arruda-Boyce λm) at P/µ = 1.5, equal positive pressures
unlisted_needs: parametric sweep over α and λm
critical separation (η/R)critical as a function of the stiffening parameter
missing_information: range and values of α and λm swept
reference_values: (η/R)critical directly but weakly proportional to λm (Arruda-Boyce)

cases.name: Linear elastic, unequal pressures P1=P, P2=0.8P
neo-Hookean, unequal pressures P1=P, P2=0.8P
unlisted_needs: no mirror symmetry between cavities (only axisymmetry possible)
reference_values: Deformed shape shown for η/R = 2.8, P/µ = 1.0
Critical η/R exists where interaction turns from attractive to repulsive

quotes: For all models, a value of µ = 20 was chosen for ABAQUS simulations. For Mooney-Rivlin, α = 0.5, and for Arruda-Boyce, λm = 2, were chosen as the constitutive model parameters.
we carry out simulations for two unequal pressures P1 ̸= P2 , choosing P1 = P and P2 = 0.8P
Representative deformed shapes of cavities for both equal positive and equal negative pressures are shown in Figure 7 for η/R=2.8 and pressure of P/µ=1.0.
Figure 8 shows the variation of potential energy, driving force, and (η/R)critical as a function of strain-stiffening parameters for a representative pressure of P/µ = 1.5.
the elastic interaction between two equi-sized pressurized spherical cavities in an infinite elastic matrix is always attractive at low pressures (P/µ ≲ 1.0)
